title: Your home starts with its rooms
intro: The home dashboard keeps the house map prominent. Choose a floor, tap a room or cycle through rooms without leaving Home.
changes: Uses the existing floor-plan viewer and saved room outlines.
Appliances appear at their real saved positions, with device state and freshness owned by Devices.
Room work markers open the room context: appliances, open tasks and current projects.
Rooms without an outline remain selectable; unavailable information is shown as unknown.
next: Select another room, open a linked task or project, or open the room itself.
connection: Places owns rooms and geometry. Devices, Energy, Tasks and Projects contribute their existing records.

title: One project, with its useful connections
intro: The project answers three questions: what is next, what do we need, and how is the budget doing?
changes: The existing project cover banner stays: the image helps identify the project immediately.
A stable header and related-record cards replace unrelated blocks and loose links.
Related records use coloured icons, counts and a whole-card tap target; phones show two cards per row.
Real task progress, residents and a clear next step make the project feel achievable.
Spent, still planned and remaining amounts have separate meanings.
next: Open Materials to see what the task needs, then open the product.
connection: Projects hosts the page; Tasks, Shopping, Inventory and Expenses provide their own records.

title: A product keeps one identity throughout the household
intro: The product page brings stock, task needs, project use, purchases and shop variants together.
changes: Three cartridges at home and two required for a task are shown as different facts.
Related views use the same product, rather than creating project-specific copies.
Household units stay practical: jars, packs and pieces do not require weights.
next: Follow the requirement into shopping, or use existing stock for the task.
connection: The catalogue owns identity; Inventory owns quantities and movements; each project relationship explains its purpose.

title: Start a trip by choosing one shop or saved group
intro: No trip-name form, preparation wizard or second list of shop checkboxes.
changes: The shared selection control puts favourites and recent choices first.
A saved group already defines its shops; users do not select them again.
The matching shopping list becomes the checklist automatically.
next: Choose the Colruyt group and press Start shopping.
connection: Shops owns destinations and groups. Shopping reuses existing needs.

title: Large, clear actions while walking through the shop
intro: The screen focuses on the items and the next useful tap.
changes: Purchased and Not now are distinct actions; skipped products do not increase stock.
Adjust opens over the checklist for planned quantity and linked variants only. Extra products and stock locations remain separate.
Extra products remain possible without leaving the trip behind.
next: Finish after resolving the checklist. Remaining open items require an explicit skip decision.
connection: Acquisitions use the existing central purchase/stock workflow once; other household members see the same session.

title: Quantity and a linked variant, without leaving the checklist
intro: Adjust is a small form over the current shopping checklist. The background and visit context remain in place.
changes: Uses the production shared form dialog and existing product picker.
Only planned quantity and variants already linked to this product appear here.
Saving a plan does not add stock or change earlier acquisitions.
Stock locations, extra products, receipts and payment keep their own actions.
next: Save to continue shopping at the same place in the checklist.
connection: The web and MCP use the same session service, stock-owner validation and item revisions.

title: Close the trip first; add evidence and payment when useful
intro: Completion leads to a short review instead of another compulsory administrative task.
changes: Review purchased quantities and stock location, including goods not tracked yet.
Link a receipt or an existing/new expense during or after the trip.
Adding a receipt or payment must not purchase the same goods again.
next: Open the linked purchase or expense whenever you need the details.
connection: Shopping owns the checklist; purchase evidence, inventory and payments keep their own responsibilities.

title: One receipt can serve a project and the household
intro: A €45 Gamma purchase allocates €35 to the bathroom and €10 to the household.
changes: Actual product lines stay visible with quantities and purpose.
Receipt, stock, expense and project links provide a traceable path.
Allocation explains a cost; it does not create another payment.
next: Open the expense to see payer, account and payment status.
connection: Acquisitions describe goods. Expenses records payment. Projects reads its allocated share.

title: Actual account balance and forecast are separate
intro: The account view explains where its balance came from and what is still expected.
changes: Actual balance, still to pay and projected balance are labelled separately.
Contributions are transfers into this account, not a second salary.
The purchase debits the account once, even when several projects share its cost.
next: Follow the expense or account-history record to understand an amount.
connection: Money composes account entries and owner-provided financial records; it does not duplicate expenses.

title: Home Assistant belongs in everyday home context
intro: Rooms, climate, lighting, devices and energy share the same household navigation.
changes: Colourful icon tiles give each area a recognisable place.
Source and freshness explain whether a value is current.
Room and device links lead to useful information and supported controls.
next: Open a room, then the actual device or its maintenance task.
connection: Home Assistant supplies live state. WickedHome features own names, spaces, maintenance and financial context.

title: Room controls follow actual device capabilities
intro: A room combines its climate, lighting and relevant tasks without becoming a separate control system.
changes: The same card, selection, state and navigation patterns continue here.
Supported controls come from the linked device; sensor-only devices do not gain imaginary buttons.
Offline or stale state stays visible and must not be presented as confirmed success.
next: Open the device for supported actions or follow its task.
connection: Devices owns identity and maintenance; Home Assistant owns the external state and command result.

title: Recipe cards keep their food covers
intro: Food images make recipes easy to recognise and pleasant to browse.
changes: Generous cover cards remain the default recipe overview.
List mode keeps the same recipes and facts, with compact thumbnails.
Missing covers use a clear recipe icon instead of a broken image.
next: Open the recipe to see its existing banner and cooking actions.
connection: Media belongs to the record owner. The overview, list and detail reuse the same image reference and shared presentation patterns.

title: The recipe banner remains part of its identity
intro: A wide cover belongs with the recipe title, facts and next action.
changes: Retain the existing recipe cover and cover chooser.
The title, stock facts and actions stay legible outside the photo.
The same product and stock relationships remain available.
next: Check requirements or start cooking from the same record.
connection: Media belongs to the record owner. The overview, list and detail reuse the same image reference and shared presentation patterns.

title: Project cards keep covers, progress and budget
intro: A project is easier to spot through its image and meaningful status.
changes: Keep project photos on cards and detail banners.
Switch to a list for denser comparison without losing context.
Progress, budget and next actions accompany the image.
next: Open the project to continue its task or inspect materials.
connection: Media belongs to the record owner. The overview, list and detail reuse the same image reference and shared presentation patterns.

title: Product photos and compact thumbnails belong in both views
intro: Product images help recognition while units, stock and links remain readable.
changes: Use the actual saved product image; keep packaging visible with contain.
The same shared card/list switch remembers your choice.
A missing product photo falls back to its domain icon; no forced upload.
next: Open the product for stock, purchases, shop variants and project use.
connection: Media belongs to the record owner. The overview, list and detail reuse the same image reference and shared presentation patterns.

title: Device photos sit beside useful state information
intro: A familiar photo helps locate the right appliance or device.
changes: Use saved device photos where available, with profile icons as fallbacks.
Location, state and source freshness remain explicit.
Controls still come from real capabilities; the photo proves no live state.
next: Open the device for its room, maintenance and supported controls.
connection: Media belongs to the record owner. The overview, list and detail reuse the same image reference and shared presentation patterns.
